subject: Re: Evidencing erasure + default capture behavior — quick clarifications
messages:
From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@finapp.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on what you keep by default (requests vs answers)

Hi Rishi,

We're finalizing the SOW language and have one last compliance check from our legal team: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default for hosted API calls? Specifically: 1) do you persist the raw user input (we call it "user_input") and 2) the model's response ("model_answer") and for how long?

Also, FinApp requires demonstrable proof of deletion in the event of an erasure request — can you outline the form of evidence you provide (audit log entries, deletion job IDs, hashes, etc.) and whether those proofs are stored in EU regions for EU customers?

Appreciate a short bullet list if possible — legal needs this for signature.

Thanks,
Emma Clarke
Security & Compliance, FinApp
emma.clarke@finapp.com
+44 20 5555 1234
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@finapp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you keep by default (requests vs answers)

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks. TL;DR bullets below, followed by a short explanation and the steps we use to produce deletion evidence. I've attached a one-page guide for legal.

- Default capture: we persist request metadata (timestamps, route, client id) and the request payload (user_input) for 30 days by default for hosted customers.
- Model outputs (model_answer) are retained for 90 days by default to support quality monitoring and regression alerts.
- Streaming fragments / ephemeral KV cache data are not retained beyond the session flux unless the session is finalized and explicitly stored by the customer.
- Evidence of deletion: we issue a deletion job with a unique job ID, store an append-only audit record (job ID, timestamp, operator/service account, scope), and compute a compact proof (SHA256 hash of the resource manifest) which we can export as a signed artifact. These artifacts are retained in the customer's residency region for 365 days to satisfy audit needs.

Notes:
- For EU-region customers, both the stored data and deletion-evidence artifacts are kept in EU data regions by default.
- Customers can set project-level flags (suppress_logs=true) or use our private deployment options to enforce zero retention of request and response payloads; in those cases, only minimal telemetry (non-identifying metrics for health) is kept.

Action items for FinApp:
1) If you want default timelines shortened (e.g., 7-day request retention), we can add that to the SOW and apply a project-level configuration.
2) If you need deletion evidence delivered via signed S3 object and a support ticket, reply and we'll generate a sample for your legal team within 48 hours.

Kimberly / Marissa — cc'ing for confirmation on the evidence artifact format and EU residency handling.

Best,
Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@finapp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you keep by default (requests vs answers)

Thanks Rishi, confirming the evidence specifics:

- Deletion Job: GUID (deletion-job-<timestamp>-<guid>) and a monotonic run id.
- Audit record fields: job_id, affected_keys (list), initiating_principal, deletion_window, storage_region, checksum_manifest (SHA256 list).
- Signed artifact: we sign the checksum_manifest using our HSM-backed key and return a small JSON file that includes the signed manifest and the audit record.

For EU customers we route these artifacts to the EU artifact store (same residency as the data) and provide a signed URL to download. We keep those artifacts for 365 days to support fintech/regulator requests. If you prefer, we can shorten the artifact retention window but that requires SI review.

Kimberly Park
